points.why: It states the question explicitly as why median and 90th-percentile door-to-discharge time keep rising, and says the boundary follows from it.
It names stocks (waiting room, treatment bays, boarders, queues) and flows (arrivals, admission, discharge, leaks).
It brings inpatient beds, discharge flow and primary-care demand inside, and explicitly calls the ED-only data a convenience boundary.
It defends each exclusion and checks for leaks (left without being seen, diversions, transfers), but never runs CATWOE or an equivalent stakeholder-perspective check.
